To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a clonal origin could not be excluded for both components of the tumour.
the clonal origin and the malignant transformation of a paediatric sPNET were established by means of LOH analysis.

1) sPNETs can be associated with malignant astroglial transformation; 2) the malignant transformation of sPNETs is characterized by LOH; 3) LOH is also detectable in sPNETs without astroglial transformation and 4) sPNET and malignant astrocytoma are clonally related.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a rare case of a sPNET with a malignant astrocytic component and the first description in the literature of a clonal origin.
the question of whether the malignant transformation of the sPNET is the consequence of a clonal evolution or whether it is the result of a de novo tumour formation.
the biological behaviour of the malignant transformation of sPNET and its clonal origin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both tumour entities, sPNET and glioblastoma, have arisen from a common stem cell and that the astrocytic component has developed from the neuroectodermal component by malignant transformation.
the sPNET and the glioblastoma are of the same clonal origin.
both components of this tumour are derived from a single cell and are thus clonally related.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a clonal origin is a common phenomenon in paediatric brain tumours and that the astrocytic transformation of a sPNET may be associated with an increased aggressiveness of the disease.
sPNETs are characterized by a high degree of heterogeneity and a clonal relationship between the different tumour areas is likely.
the malignant transformation of sPNETs is a very rare phenomenon and that the clonal origin has been demonstrated for the first time in this case.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the clonal origin and the malignant transformation of sPNETs may have a role in the aggressive biological behaviour of these tumours and should therefore be considered as a possible explanation for their recurrence and progression.
the malignant transformation of a sPNET to a glioblastoma is a rare event.
the presence of anaplastic or glioblastoma components within a sPNET does not necessarily imply a different origin of both components.
